idiom_name: createContext<T | null>(null) + useX() accessor/hook that throws when unprovided
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds a generic and a discipline on top of the React realisation: createContext<Theme | null>(null) types the reader, but the type cannot express that a provider must exist above it, so the idiomatic wrapper is a small useTheme() hook that reads the context and throws (or asserts) when the value is null. The provider side is unchanged - React 19 accepts <Ctx value={...}>, older versions need <Ctx.Provider> - and the value identity rules that drive re-renders are the same as in JavaScript.
pitfalls: Casting the default with `undefined as any` or a non-null assertion moves the missing-provider failure from a clear message to a crash inside an unrelated component.
The generic does not make the provider mandatory, so previews, stories and tests can silently fall back to the default value.
Two context objects with the same value type are still different identities - TypeScript's structural typing happily accepts a value meant for another context.

variants.name: Typed AsyncLocalStorage store for a request flow
variants.implementation_notes: On the server TypeScript types the store instead of the tree: new AsyncLocalStorage<RequestStore>() documents exactly what a request flow publishes, run(store, callback) binds it for one asynchronous operation and getStore() returns RequestStore | undefined - so the reader must decide between a default and an error, unlike the React variant where the type of the value alone can be non-nullable. The mechanics (context propagated through continuations and promise chains, nothing re-rendered) are the JavaScript ones.
pitfalls: getStore() returns undefined for code running outside a run() scope, so every reader needs an explicit fallback decision instead of assuming a store exists.
Typing the store does not prevent mutation: a shared object put into the store is global state with a request-shaped name.
Mixing AsyncLocalStorage with libraries that drop the async context (native addons, some emitters) yields undefined in the middle of an otherwise correct flow.
